headline: EFCC Returns Unremitted Statutory Payments To The Federal Account
seoTitle: EFCC Recovers Funds From Two Oil Firms
metaDescription: Nigeria's anti-corruption agency has recovered millions in unremitted statutory payments from two oil firms and transferred the funds to the RMAFC.
aiSummaryBullets: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission recovered $3 million and N1.3 billion from two oil companies.
The seized funds originated from outstanding statutory payment liabilities owed to the Nigerian federation.
Officials formally transferred the collected revenue to the Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission.
aiContextParagraph: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) recently secured the recovery of financial assets totaling $3 million and N1.3 billion from two distinct entities within the oil sector, identified as Aiteo and Newcross. According to statements released by the agency, these funds represent the settlement of long-standing liabilities linked to unremitted statutory payments owed to the federal government. Following the recovery process, the EFCC transitioned the funds to the Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), which is the government body responsible for monitoring the accruals and disbursement of revenue from the federation account. This enforcement action highlights ongoing efforts by state authorities to reclaim outstanding revenues from private enterprises operating within Nigeria's extractives industry. The transfer marks the completion of the agency's immediate involvement in the specific case, ensuring the redirected capital is integrated back into official government accounts.
whyItIsViral: The story gained traction through reports from two major independent national outlets, reflecting institutional accountability actions within the oil sector.
